steps: The closeness of repeated measurements to one another is called consistency of results.
items.finalAnswer: Consistency of results means that repeated measurements are close to one another.

steps: SI units are based on the decimal system.
Their multiples and submultiples are expressed using powers of ten, so converting from one unit to another is easy.
items.finalAnswer: SI units are user friendly because their decimal system makes unit conversions easy.

steps: A systematic error is an error that affects measurements in the same direction each time, making them consistently too high or too low.
A random error is an error that causes measurements to vary unpredictably from one measurement to another.
items.finalAnswer: Systematic errors affect measurements consistently in one direction, while random errors cause unpredictable variations.

steps: Random errors are caused by unpredictable changes in measuring conditions or by limitations in the observer’s ability to make measurements.
items.finalAnswer: Random errors result from unpredictable variations in measuring conditions or observation.

steps: Yes. A systematic error makes measurements consistently higher or lower than the true value, so it affects accuracy.
items.finalAnswer: Yes, a systematic error affects accuracy by shifting measurements away from the true value.

steps: The other systems of measurement used are the CGS system (centimetre, gram and second) and the British Engineering system (foot, pound and second).
items.finalAnswer: The CGS and British Engineering systems are also used.

steps: The metre is the distance travelled by light in vacuum during a time interval of 1/299,792,458 of a second.
items.finalAnswer: One metre is the distance travelled by light in vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second.

steps: SI units provide scientists throughout the world with a common, internationally accepted system of measurement.
They make it easier for scientists to communicate and compare their results without confusion.
items.finalAnswer: SI units give scientists a common system and make communication and comparison of results easier.
